cluster_summary: The cluster comprises vulnerabilities in OAuth2 and OIDC clients where the callback processing fails to properly validate or bind security parameters such as state, nonce, and PKCE challenge/verifier, enabling attacks including cross-site request forgery, authorization code injection, and secret leakage. Some members also involve mass assignment and vault misconfiguration related to OAuth flows.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Remove the @ModelAttribute annotation and retrieve the server-managed AuthorizationRequest from the model map, ensuring only intended server-controlled fields are used..

sub_patterns.name: Mass assignment on OAuth authorization request object
sub_patterns.root_cause: The controller uses @ModelAttribute annotation to bind HTTP request parameters directly to an AuthorizationRequest object without an allowlist, allowing attackers to set sensitive fields such as scope or redirect_uri.
